description: We are a multidisciplinary team of students passionate about science, engineering, technology, and space exploration. Combining interests in electronics, programming, physics, biology, and data analysis, we aim to explore how NASA Earth observation data can support smarter and more sustainable agricultural decisions. We value creativity, collaboration, and practical problem-solving, and we are excited to turn scientific information into useful tools for real-world challenges.
summary:
AGROSYNC is an interactive agricultural decision-support platform developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data."

Focused on Veracruz, Mexico, AGROSYNC combines NASA POWER agroclimatic data, Open-Meteo weather information, INEGI geographic data, and agricultural knowledge to help users explore crop characteristics, environmental conditions, and sustainable crop rotation strategies.

Through interactive tools such as the Regions explorer, Crop Index, and Rotation Advisor, users can compare agricultural scenarios and better understand the relationship between crops, soil, and water.

AGROSYNC aims to make Earth observation data and agricultural knowledge more accessible, supporting informed exploration of sustainable farming practices. It is an educational decision-support tool, not a substitute for professional agronomic advice or field measurements.
details:
AGROSYNC is a web-based agricultural decision-support platform designed to help users explore sustainable crop rotation strategies in Veracruz, Mexico.

The platform combines geographic information from INEGI, daily agroclimatic data from NASA POWER, and weather information from Open-Meteo. These sources provide environmental context for exploring agricultural scenarios.

AGROSYNC includes several interactive sections:

  • Regions: Allows users to explore municipalities and localities in Veracruz and consult available environmental information.
  • Crop Index: Presents information about selected crops and their characteristics.
  • Rotation Advisor: Compares crop rotation scenarios using agricultural criteria such as root systems, nitrogen fixation, water requirements, and ecological suitability.
  • Guides and Vivarium: Provide educational material about soil health, water management, crop biology, and sustainable agricultural practices.

The platform was developed using Python, Flask, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and JSON.

AGROSYNC aims to make Earth observation data and agricultural knowledge more accessible to students and people interested in sustainable agriculture.

Limitations: NASA POWER provides gridded agroclimatic information rather than parcel-level measurements. Weather information is based on model estimates. Agricultural criteria are intended for educational exploration and do not replace laboratory soil analysis, field measurements, or professional agronomic advice.
